title: Repeat system outage, furious customer, critical escalation
notes: High-emotion repeat caller. Exercises the extreme sentiment value, a critical priority, error-code extraction, and an escalated status. All data is synthetic.
transcript: Speaker 1: SSM Repak technical support, this is Daan. How can I help?
Speaker 2: Finally. This is Robert King, account AC-10092, and this is the third time I've called this week. Your system keeps going down and it's costing me real money.
Speaker 1: I'm very sorry, Robert. I can hear how frustrating this is. Can you tell me exactly what's happening now?
Speaker 2: The whole production line management system is offline. It throws "SYS-900 service unavailable" and then nothing. My factory is at a standstill.
Speaker 1: Understood. A full system outage stopping production is critical, and I'm treating it as critical priority right now.
Speaker 2: I don't want priorities, I want it fixed. I've been told that twice already and nothing changed.

Speaker 1: I hear you. I'm not going to give you another holding answer. The SYS-900 error is a backend service failure, that's beyond what I can restart from here. I'm escalating this directly to our engineering team as a critical incident, and I'm staying on the case as your point of contact.
Speaker 2: And what does that actually mean for me?
Speaker 1: It means an engineer is assigned immediately, not queued. I'll personally call you with an update within the hour. What number should I use?
Speaker 2: 06 99887766. Within the hour, I'm holding you to that.
Speaker 1: Understood. I've logged a critical incident for the SYS-900 outage and escalated it to engineering. I'll call you on that number within the hour.
